newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Triodos Bank plans Dfl20 mln share issue.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Triodos Bank plans Dfl20 mln share issue.

text.p: Dutch ethical bank Triodos Bank NV said on Wednesday it planned to double its capital by issuing at least 20 million guilders of non-voting shares.
Spokesman Thomas Steiner said five percent shareholder Delta Lloyd and co-operative bank Rabobank Nederland BA had indicated they would take up shares in the issue.
He said this would give them stakes of between five and 7.5 percent in the enlarged capital of the bank, which invests in "green" projects such as wind power and organic farming.
"For the growth of the bank, it's necessary that we have stronger capital," Steiner told Reuters.
He said assets had grown at 30 percent per year in recent years.
A Rabobank spokesman confirmed his bank's investment plans but a spokesman for Delta Lloyd declined to comment.
The voting shares of Triodos Bank, formed in 1980, are owned by a foundation governed by six directors.
The non-voting share issue, the fifth in its history, is being offered to retail and institutional investors.
The bank has branches in Britain, Belgium and the Netherlands.
